g.text: A state IS a BFD session state (RFC 5880 §6.2); the local value of bfd.SessionState
Session-establishment transition — the three-way handshake climbing Down → Init → Up (RFC 5880 §6.8.6)
Session teardown on failure — peer signalled Down/AdminDown, Detection Time expired, or the Echo function failed (RFC 5880 §6.8.4, §6.8.5, §6.8.6)
Administrative control — an operator action from outside BFD, not a received packet (RFC 5880 §6.8.16)
No state change: the event has a defined outcome and that outcome is to stay put (RFC 5880 §6.8.6)
RFC 5880 §6.8.6 transition function — every (state, event) pair has a defined outcome
Administrative control (RFC 5880 §6.8.16) — outside the packet-reception rules
set LocalDiag; cease sending BFD Echo packets

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown # Genre: statechart — EXPERIMENTAL, and it needs `figdown 0.2` (`STATECHART-GENRE-SCOPE`). The two # companion TABLE sections below stay `figdown 0.1`: the version a section # declares is the surface that section needs, and a table needs nothing from # 0.2. Sections are separate documents (`MULTI-FIGURE-DOCUMENTS`), so the versions may differ. figdown 0.2 statechart title "BFD Session State Machine (RFC 5880 §6.2)" # ── What this figure is ───────────────────────────────────────────── # The BFD session state machine transcribed from RFC 5880 (Katz & Ward, # June 2010) — from the RFC ITSELF, §6.2's own ASCII diagram plus the # normative prose, not from any vendor restatement of it. # # WHY THAT PROVENANCE IS WORTH A COMMENT. Downstream transcriptions of # this machine circulate with THREE states (Down, Init, Up), treating # AdminDown only as a value that can arrive in a received packet. # RFC 5880 §6.2 is explicit that there are FOUR: "There are three states # through which a session normally proceeds: two for establishing a # session (Init and Up) and one for tearing down a session (Down) … # A fourth state (AdminDown) exists so that a session can be # administratively put down indefinitely." AdminDown is BOTH a local # session state and a value carried in the State (Sta) field — §4.1 # encodes Sta as 0=AdminDown, 1=Down, 2=Init, 3=Up — and conflating the # two is exactly the error this figure exists to not repeat. # # WHICH TEXT GOVERNS. §6.2's diagram is a summary and says so: it notes # "Transitions involving AdminDown state are deleted for clarity (but # are fully specified in sections 6.8.6 and 6.8.16)." So the diagram is # transcribed here for its three states' arcs, and §6.8.6 (Reception of # BFD Control Packets), §6.8.4/§6.8.5 (detection-time and Echo failure) # and §6.8.16 (Administrative Control) supply the rest. Where the two # disagree, the prose wins; see the DOWN self-loop note below, which is # the one place they do. # # Notation on every transition label follows the RFC's own: the arc # names the state of the REMOTE system as received in the State field, # or the expiry of the Detection Timer. `rx X` = a BFD Control packet # arrived carrying Sta = X. # HONEST LIMIT (guide/expressing.md known limits — "closed-world readings"; the # genre's own reading rule 5, spec/genres/experimental/statechart.md): # the transition function is TOTAL and this figure cannot say so. # RFC 5880 §6.8.6 defines an outcome for EVERY (local state, received # Sta) pair — sixteen of them, plus a defined outcome for the Detection # Timer in every state. Nothing is left to the implementer. That # TOTALITY is a fact about the machine, and it is the fact a decision # table asserts structurally: every cell is filled, so a reader can see # at a glance that nothing was forgotten. # # A transition graph with merged triggers cannot assert it. The # statechart genre's reading rules say a reader may conclude that "the # state set is closed as drawn", but adds in the same breath that # "absence is still not prohibition — a transition not drawn is not # stated to be forbidden". That is the gap, stated by the genre itself: # there is NO construct — no keyword, no option key, no annotation — # that lets an author claim "the pairs not drawn here are not missing; # they are the pairs whose defined outcome is no state change". A # reading agent therefore cannot distinguish a deliberately-omitted # pair from a forgotten one, and neither can a human. # # What this figure does INSTEAD, and it is a workaround, not the # construct: (a) it draws the three no-change self-loops the RFC's own # diagram draws, plus the fourth (AdminDown) that the RFC omits for # clarity, so every state visibly answers for the events that leave it # unmoved; and (b) it carries the full 4×5 decision table as a # companion `table` section below — composition, the same interim # `tcp-handshake.fd` uses to carry lifeline state that `topology` has # no construct for. The table asserts totality by being complete. The # statechart above does not assert it at all; a reader gets it from the # panel or from the prose, never from the model. # ── Semantic classes — meaning first, colour is only render ────────── class states "A state IS a BFD session state (RFC 5880 §6.2); the local value of bfd.SessionState" fill=#eef2ff class advance "Session-establishment transition — the three-way handshake climbing Down → Init → Up (RFC 5880 §6.8.6)" stroke=#16a34a class fail "Session teardown on failure — peer signalled Down/AdminDown, Detection Time expired, or the Echo function failed (RFC 5880 §6.8.4, §6.8.5, §6.8.6)" stroke=#dc2626 class admin "Administrative control — an operator action from outside BFD, not a received packet (RFC 5880 §6.8.16)" stroke=#9333ea style=dashed class hold "No state change: the event has a defined outcome and that outcome is to stay put (RFC 5880 §6.8.6)" stroke=#64748b style=dotted # ── The four states (RFC 5880 §6.2; Sta encoding from §4.1) ────────── state down "DOWN\nSta=1" shape=rounded class=states # Session is down, or has just been created. §6.2: it remains Down until # the remote system agrees the session is down by sending State other # than Up. Semantically the forwarding path is unavailable. A system MAY # hold a session here indefinitely by simply refusing to advance. state init "INIT\nSta=2" shape=rounded class=states # The remote system is communicating and the local system wants the # session up, but the remote system does not yet realise it. §6.2. state up "UP\nSta=3" shape=rounded class=states # The session is established; connectivity between the systems is # working. §6.2. state admindown "ADMINDOWN\nSta=0" shape=rounded class=states # Held administratively down. §6.2: this causes the REMOTE system to # enter Down and remain there until the local system leaves AdminDown, # and it has no semantic implication for the availability of the # forwarding path. §6.8.6 discards every received packet while here, so # no arriving packet can move the session out — only §6.8.16 can. # `down` rather than the genre default `right`: this machine climbs # Down → Init → Up and falls back the same way, so the reading axis is # the ladder. `flow right` was tried and rejected on the render — it # packs all four states into one row and the merged trigger labels pile # up on each other around INIT. flow down # NO LAYOUT ZONE, AND THAT IS A FORCED CHOICE, NOT A PREFERENCE. # Every RFC-faithful FSM figure in this repository is hand-pinned, and # this one cannot be: the engine draws a self-transition as a small side # loop ONLY when neither endpoint is pinned. Pin any state here and its # self-transition degenerates to a zero-length line at the state's # centre, with the trigger label printed on top of the state's own name # — all four self-loops vanish and all four state names are obliterated. # That was built and looked at before this comment was written. Since # all four states carry a self-transition, there is no partial pinning # that escapes it, so the figure takes the automatic layout and the # render defects noted at the foot of this file. # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # TRANSITIONS — triggers MERGED onto shared arcs # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # The point of the graph over the table: §6.8.6 has fewer distinct # state changes than the table has cells. Of the totality table's # twenty cells (four states × five events), NINE are state changes — # and those nine collapse onto FIVE arcs, plus the four no-change # self-loops that carry the other eleven cells, because several events # share one outcome: "rx AdminDown", "Detect Time expired" and "Echo # failed" all mean Up → Down, and the RFC writes them in three separate # sections. The four ADMINISTRATIVE arcs below are not among those # twenty cells at all — §6.8.16 sits outside the packet-reception rules # and has its own table. Thirteen `transition` lines in total: 5 + 4 # state-changing, 4 self-loops. # # WHY "Echo failed" IS DRAWN ON TWO ARCS AND HAS NO COLUMN. It is # §6.8.5, and the Echo function is not active in every state, so the RFC # defines no outcome for it in every row. A totality table asserts # totality by having every cell filled, and a column whose cells the RFC # leaves undefined would break exactly the claim the table exists to # make. So Echo failure rides on the teardown arcs, where §6.8.5 does # define it, and the table stays the grid it can honestly fill. # ── Climbing: the three-way handshake (§6.8.6) ────────────────────── transition down -[rx Down]-> init class=advance # §6.8.6: "If bfd.SessionState is Down / If received State is Down / # Set bfd.SessionState to Init". The peer agrees the session is down. transition down -[rx Init]-> up class=advance # §6.8.6: "Else if received State is Init / Set bfd.SessionState to Up". # The peer is already one step ahead, so Down goes straight to Up. transition init -[rx Init, rx Up]-> up class=advance # §6.8.6: "Else if bfd.SessionState is Init / If received State is Init # or Up / Set bfd.SessionState to Up". Two triggers, one outcome — # merged onto one arc rather than drawn twice. Matches the RFC diagram's # own arc label "INIT, UP". # ── Falling: teardown (§6.8.4, §6.8.5, §6.8.6) ────────────────────── transition init -["rx AdminDown\nDetect expired, Echo failed"]-> down class=fail # Three sources, one arc. §6.8.6: received AdminDown while # bfd.SessionState is not Down sets LocalDiag 3 (Neighbor signaled # session down) and the state to Down. §6.8.4: Detection Time passes # without a packet while the state is Init or Up — LocalDiag 1 (Control # Detection Time Expired). §6.8.5: Echo function failed — LocalDiag 2. transition up -["rx Down, rx AdminDown\nDetect expired, Echo failed"]-> down class=fail # The same three, plus received Down: §6.8.6 "Else (bfd.SessionState is # Up) / If received State is Down / Set bfd.LocalDiag to 3 … Set # bfd.SessionState to Down". Four triggers, one arc. The RFC diagram # writes this arc "ADMIN DOWN, DOWN, TIMER"; Echo failure is §6.8.5, # which the diagram does not cover at all. # ── Administrative control (§6.8.16) — not a received packet ──────── transition down -[admin disable]-> admindown class=admin transition init -[admin disable]-> admindown class=admin transition up -[admin disable]-> admindown class=admin # §6.8.16: "Else / Set bfd.SessionState to AdminDown / Set # bfd.LocalDiag to an appropriate value / Cease the transmission of BFD # Echo packets". Drawn from all three other states because the RFC puts # no precondition on it. These are the arcs §6.2's diagram deletes for # clarity, and the reason a three-state transcription looks complete. transition admindown -[admin enable]-> down class=admin # §6.8.16: "If enabling session / Set bfd.SessionState to Down". The # ONLY way out of AdminDown — §6.8.6 discards every received packet # while the session is AdminDown, so no peer can lift it. # ── No-change self-loops: the defined outcome is "stay put" ───────── transition down -["rx Up, rx AdminDown\nDetect expired"]-> down class=hold # The RFC diagram draws this self-loop and labels it exactly # "UP, ADMIN DOWN, TIMER". # # WHERE THE DIAGRAM AND THE PROSE DISAGREE, AND THE PROSE WINS. The # diagram's self-loop suggests an event with an effect. §6.8.6 says # otherwise for all three: received Up while Down falls through every # branch (Down handles only received Down and received Init), received # AdminDown is guarded by "If bfd.SessionState is not Down" and so does # nothing at all here — not even the LocalDiag write — and §6.8.4 arms # the timer only when the state is Init or Up. So all three are # genuinely no-ops, and this arc is drawn to say that they are DEFINED # no-ops rather than gaps. This is the one place the summary diagram # and the normative text read differently. transition init -[rx Down]-> init class=hold # §6.8.6's Init branch handles received Init and Up only; received Down # falls through, so the session stays in Init. The RFC diagram draws # this self-loop and labels it "DOWN". transition up -[rx Init, rx Up]-> up class=hold # §6.8.6's Up branch handles received Down only; Init and Up fall # through. The RFC diagram draws this self-loop and labels it # "INIT, UP". transition admindown -[any packet: discarded]-> admindown class=hold # §6.8.6, first clause after the header checks: "If bfd.SessionState is # AdminDown / Discard the packet". Every received Sta value, and the # Detection Timer too (§6.8.4 fires only in Init or Up). The RFC's # diagram cannot show this — it deletes AdminDown entirely — so this # arc is present here and absent there, deliberately. # ── RENDER DEFECTS PRESENT IN THE PUBLISHED ARTIFACT ──────────────── # Recorded rather than papered over. These are engine render defects, # not limits of the language, and the figure ships with them visible: # # 1. SELF-LOOP LABEL STRUCK BY ITS OWN LOOP. The trigger label of a # self-transition is centred on the loop's outer stroke, so the loop # draws through the text. Visible on INIT ("rx Down"), on UP # ("rx Init, rx Up") and on ADMINDOWN ("any packet: discarded"). # The DOWN self-loop escapes it only because its label is two lines. # 2. UP's self-loop label is struck a SECOND time, by the long # Up → Down teardown edge running horizontally through it. # 3. The three back edges into DOWN (from INIT, from UP, from # ADMINDOWN) route out to a side channel far to the right, so their # labels sit a long way from the states they connect. Correct, and # hard to follow. # 4. Crowding at INIT: the "rx Init" label of Down → Up lands against # INIT's box edge and immediately above INIT's own self-loop label. # # Nothing below this line changes any of that; see the `flow` note above # for why the usual fix (pin the states) is unavailable here. # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # COMPANION TABLE — the totality the statechart cannot assert # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # Sections are separate documents, so this one declares the version its # own surface needs: a table needs nothing from 0.2. # # Read this as the structural claim the figure above cannot make: every # cell is filled, therefore §6.8.6 leaves no pair undefined. Twenty # cells; nine of them are state changes and eleven are defined no-ops. # Delete this section and the machine above is unchanged — and the # assertion "nothing is missing" is gone with it. figdown 0.1 table table transitions "RFC 5880 §6.8.6 transition function — every (state, event) pair has a defined outcome" | bfd.SessionState | rx Sta=0 AdminDown | rx Sta=1 Down | rx Sta=2 Init | rx Sta=3 Up | Detect Time expired (§6.8.4) | |------------------|--------------------|---------------|---------------|-------------|------------------------------| | DOWN (1) | stay DOWN
(guarded: no diag) | → INIT | → UP | stay DOWN | stay DOWN
(timer runs only in Init/Up) | | INIT (2) | → DOWN
diag 3 | stay INIT | → UP | → UP | → DOWN
diag 1 | | UP (3) | → DOWN
diag 3 | → DOWN
diag 3 | stay UP | stay UP | → DOWN
diag 1 | | ADMINDOWN (0) | discard | discard | discard | discard | stay ADMINDOWN | figdown 0.1 table table admin "Administrative control (RFC 5880 §6.8.16) — outside the packet-reception rules" | Action | From | To | Also | |------------------|-----------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------| | enable session | ADMINDOWN | DOWN | the only exit from ADMINDOWN | | disable session | DOWN, INIT, UP | ADMINDOWN | set LocalDiag; cease sending BFD Echo packets |
